choices: Nothing — a `// Brave:` comment helps resolve conflicts during rebases
Keep only `BRAVE_FOO_INIT`; drop the comment, blank line and whitespace fix
Keep the comment but revert the trailing-whitespace fix to shrink the hunk
Move the comment above the function signature so it doesn't touch the body
explain: Patches contain only the minimal functional change — no comments, blank lines or whitespace fixes. Every extra line is more to review and more to conflict on Chromium upgrades.

prompt: You need to inject about 8 lines of Brave logic into the middle of an upstream `.cc` function. Which approach follows the patch guidelines?
choices: A multiline patch inserting the 8 lines, wrapped in `// Brave start` / `// Brave end` markers
Several small 2–3 line patches spread through the function so each hunk rebases easily
Copy the upstream function's body into the patch as a replacement block
Move the logic into a macro or `chromium_src` override and patch in one line
explain: Never create multiline hand-written patches. Move the logic into a `#define` or `chromium_src` override so the patch itself stays one line.

prompt: A patch adds three Brave entries to a list/block in an upstream file, and more Brave entries are expected later. How should the patch be written?
choices: Patch in an `include` of a Brave-owned file that holds the entries
Add all three entries inline and update the patch whenever new ones are needed
Create one patch file per entry so each can be dropped independently
Replace the upstream list entirely with a Brave-maintained copy of it
explain: When a patch adds to a list or block, use an `include` so future items are added in brave-core without touching the patch again.

prompt: You must make `PermissionControllerImpl::GetPermissionStatus` return early for a Brave-specific permission. Which patch line is preferred?
choices: `+  if (permission == AUTOPLAY) return true;` as a single inline line
`+  // Brave: AUTOPLAY early return` followed by the inline `if` check
`+BRAVE_PERMISSION_CONTROLLER_IMPL_GET_PERMISSION_STATUS`, defined in brave-core
`+#define BRAVE_HOOK if (permission == AUTOPLAY) return true;` written inside the patch
explain: Patches should reference a `#define` whose body lives in brave-core, so behavior can change without editing the patch. Name it `BRAVE_ALL_CAPS_ORIGINAL_METHOD_NAME`.

prompt: An upstream Android layout XML contains a `<LinearLayout>` block that Brave doesn't want. How should the patch get rid of it?
choices: Delete the element's lines with `-` lines so the patch clearly shows what's removed
Wrap the block in an XML comment: add a `<!--` line before and `-->` after
Add `android:visibility="gone"` to the opening tag so it never renders
Delete it and re-add an empty `<LinearLayout/>` placeholder for ID lookups
explain: In XML patches, comment out with `<!-- -->` instead of deleting lines. That keeps the patch addition-only and minimizes the diff.

prompt: Your one-line patch to an upstream `.cc` file comes out at 104 characters. A reviewer points out the 80-column limit. Best response?
choices: Split it over two lines, since patched files must pass the 80-column lint
Shorten it by renaming the upstream variables it references to fit 80 columns
Run `git cl format` on the upstream file so the line wraps automatically
Keep it on one line; lint doesn't run on patches, and one-liners rebase better
explain: Keep patches to one line even if that breaks the line-length limit, because lint doesn't run on patched files. Also put additions on separate lines and match existing code exactly so the patch auto-resolves.

prompt:
Brave needs to drop a dependency from an upstream target:

```gn
  public_deps += [ ":chrome_framework_widevine_signature" ]
```

Which patch is preferred?
choices: Add a line: `public_deps -= [ ":chrome_framework_widevine_signature" ]`
Delete the original `public_deps +=` line with a `-` line in the patch
Comment out the original line with `#` so it's easy to restore later
Change the original line to `public_deps += []` to keep line numbers stable
explain: Use `-=` on a separate line to remove items from GN lists. The patch then only adds a line and never modifies the original one.

prompt: A patch to an upstream `BUILD.gn` target needs to add `//brave/browser/ui/views/location_bar` as a dep, and more Brave deps will likely follow. Which patch line is best?
choices: `+  deps += [ "//brave/browser/ui/views/location_bar" ]`
`+  deps += [ ... ]` listing every Brave dep you can foresee now
`+  deps += brave_browser_window_deps`, defined in Brave code
`+  public_deps = [ "//brave/browser/ui" ]`, replacing the upstream deps
explain: Define a variable in Brave code and patch only the reference to it. Deps can then be added or removed without touching the patch.

prompt: To change how upstream's `java_cpp_enum.py` generates a Java enum, a teammate adds a patch to the Python script. Your review?
choices: Fine — Python scripts aren't compiled, so the patch is low risk
Don't patch build scripts; patch the enum's header instead
Fine, as long as the Python patch is a single, macro-style line
Guard the patched code with an environment-variable check so it only runs for Brave
explain: Patching Python build scripts prevents correct incremental rebuilds and breaks remote `siso` actions. Prefer a `chromium_src` override or a `#define`. For enums processed by upstream scripts, a multiline header patch is acceptable.
